model: annealed soda-lime glass: 1000 MPa squeezed, 40 MPa stretched; heel = square glass post 1 cm x 1 cm, 4 cm tall; Gus 80 kg; a running step = 2.5 body weights tilted 10 degrees against the post

facts_with_sources.compressive: Viridian TechDirect 'Thermal stress / glass strength': compressive strength nominally around 1000 MPa; to shatter a 1 cm cube of glass a load of about 10 t is required. Same statement in Saint-Gobain Glass UK, 'The strength of glass'. Guardian Glass lists 700-900 MPa.
facts_with_sources.tensile: Viridian: resistance to breakage on deflection approximately 40 MPa for annealed glass. EN 572-1: characteristic bending strength of float glass 45 N/mm2. MIT OCW 3.071 lecture 8: practical strength is limited by stress concentration at surface flaws (Griffith cracks).
facts_with_sources.running: Peak vertical ground reaction force in running is two to three times body weight (running biomechanics literature, e.g. the review in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology 2024).
facts_with_sources.elephants: African bush elephant: adult males average about 6 t, females about 3 t.
facts_with_sources.concrete: Ordinary structural concrete: compressive strength 20-40 MPa.
facts_with_sources.leicester: 'Cinderella's Shattered Dreams', Journal of Physics Special Topics, University of Leicester, 2015: a glass heel has to be lower than 1.15 cm to survive a run.
